evidence: Item::Get(unsigned short) 003D0EAC / TryGet 003D10A0 / IsExist 003D1170 walk the loaded Item archives: an archive holds numbers first..first+count-1, where first = record 0's +0x14 (block+0x1C) and count = the u16 at block+0x6; record = block+0x8+(n-first)*0x68. Item::IsDownload 00528E68 = number >= the resident archive's count, so new resident records stay non-download. Only ItemEnumerator::Enumerate also reads the archive list, and it loops to the stored count. Names: Item::Get(const char*) 003D0E90 looks the IID_ up in the global label dictionary, which ArchiveConstruct(void*,IdentHash*) 00165EEC fills from every exported label of the file after applying all its relocations (any number of both). Saves keep item numbers as u16 (unit::Item::Serialize 0044BBB4; shop::Data::Serialize 0053A4F0 writes a list of {u16 item, u8, u8} with a u8 length per shop, four shops). No fixed array or bit set sized by the item count found (scan: evidence.py --bitsets finds only GameProfile::UpdateReliance's 256-person set). Caveat: item DLC archives (GameData/Item/*.bin.lz via Item::Load 003D0F9C) number their items from the resident count too, so an appended item takes a number such an archive would use; the build refuses appends when such files exist in the RomFS (refuse_if_files; the cartridge has none, and DLC content lives outside it, so an item mod and item DLC must not be used together).

Job::Get(unsigned short) 00341AA4 / TryGet 00341CB4 / IsExist 00341D44: first = record 0's +0x18 (block+0x20), count = the u16 at block+0x6, record = block+0x8+(n-first)*0x80; Job::IsDownload compares with the resident count like Item, and class DLC archives (GameData/Job/%s.bin.lz, Job::Load) number from it too (same caveat as Item). Only JobEnumerator::Enumerate also reads the archive list. Saves store the class by number (Job::SerializePointer). No fixed array or bit set sized by the class count found (evidence.py --bitsets). Not checked in game; a new class also needs its own entries in tables this build does not change (class-change lists, models, TerrainCost row through move_cost_class, which must name an existing row).

GameProfile::UpdateReliance 0019B274 keeps a 256-bit set on the stack indexed by person number (cmp number, #256; ldrb [sp, number asr #3]); the resident Person archive already holds 255 people (numbers 0..254), so a new person would get number 255 at best and any second one falls outside the set. The support (Reliance) lists after the Person records are variable-length data indexed per person (Reliance::Load 004F11F8), not mapped yet.
per-chapter Person archives all number their people from 0x7A00 and are loaded one chapter at a time (Person::LoadArchive); not reviewed for appends
EquipSkill::Initialize gets two counts (GameData header +0x14 common, +0x18 total) and skills are also stored as bits in Person.skill_mask; not reviewed for appends
